item: Two damage-registry tests and a verify test no longer go red when the garbage collector logs another test's abandoned connection into them
summary: Cross-head red in the Core-only job of #1680 (docs only): test_a_record_that_cannot_be_written_says_the_class_and_the_errno_name_never_the_message_or_the_path asserted no traceback over ALL caplog records, and twelve sqlalchemy.pool.impl.SingletonThreadPool ERROR records with a traceback (six connections made in one thread, finalized by the garbage collector in the test's own, where SQLite refuses the rollback) had landed in it. The assertions now judge only the registry's own logger (src.database.damage; src.database.verify for the two in test_database_verify.py) and require the filtered list to be non-empty; test_with_the_pause_off_the_log_does_not_say_the_writers_are_paused, which unpacked the only ERROR record, filters by logger the same way. Proved by injecting a stranger sqlalchemy.pool ERROR with a traceback into the call phase: the old assertions fail on all three tests and the new pass; a mutant that makes damage.py (the write-failure warning) or verify.py (the start-up warning) log a traceback is still killed. The same shape in test_article_indexes, test_engine_text, test_failure_scrub, test_import_checkpoint, test_newsletter_export, test_failed_thread_start_routes_answer_409 and test_bulletin_sink_sites_rest is named as a finding for their owners. Product code unchanged.
